text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Friday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
JERUSALEM POST
- Peace hopes pinned on return of U.S. Mideast envoy Dennis Ross.
- Israeli army tries to calm situation in northern Israel.
- Government mulls anti-monopoly drive.
- Vietnam, Israel sign agriculture pact.
GLOBES
- Government to discuss structural changes and economic reforms at Sunday cabinet meeting.
- Government puts off discussion of proposal to cancel Bezeq Communications monopoly.
HAARETZ
- Effort to arrange meeting of U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright with Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat.
- Finance Minister Yaacov Neeman to ask inner cabinet for a deep cut in defence budget for 1998.
- Hebron gunman Noam Friedman to stand military trial.
- Treasury to propose government open the market in medicines to import and competition.
MAARIV
- Work committees in ultimatum to government: If you decide to privatise -- we'll go on strike.
- Netanyahu's director-general Avigdor Lieberman says: "I don't like to suck up to Arabs".
- Shas member of parliament Arye Deri says: "Racism is in the blood of ultra-Orthodox Ashkenazis".
- Hebron settlers get ok to build more units.
YEDIOTH AHRONOTH

- Prime Minister: Arafat is behaving like Saddam Hussein. Attorney gneral sets up secret team to prepare Israeli stance in negotiations on final status that includes possibility of removing Jewish settlements.

- Dahaf Poll of 501 Israelis on Thursday asked if Israel must or must not halt the peace process with the Palestinians or renew it: 32 percent favoured halting it, 66 percent renewing and 2 percent had no response.
